title: Change Data Capture (CDC) & Event Sourcing Pipeline
problem: Maintaining consistency between primary transactional databases and downstream search indexes, caches, and analytical stores using batch polling generates excessive database load and introduces unacceptable propagation latency. Polling-based architectures fail to capture intermediate updates and cannot provide reliable audit trails. A Change Data Capture pipeline overcomes these limitations by streaming row-level mutations directly from the database write-ahead log into a partitioned event broker, enabling real-time event dissemination across downstream consumers with low latency and idempotent deduplication guarantees.
use_cases: Synchronizing search indexes with transactional relational databases in real time
Invalidating distributed application cache layers immediately upon database row mutation
Streaming transactional events to audit stores and downstream analytical warehouses
hard_parts: Configuring PostgreSQL logical decoding and write-ahead log slot management without causing disk saturation during consumer downtime
Enforcing idempotent consumer writes to prevent duplicate record processing during network partitions and consumer rebalances
Handling upstream database schema migrations without terminating active Kafka Connect streaming connectors
Maintaining event ordering across horizontal consumer instances when processing multi-row transactions
screener_signals: Reproducible Docker Compose environment running PostgreSQL with wal_level=logical, Kafka, and Debezium
Demonstrated sub-second end-to-end synchronization from PostgreSQL mutations to Elasticsearch search documents
Anti-fake verification script validating dynamic column mutations and live search index reflections

components.name: Transactional Source Database
components.purpose: Stores application entities and writes row-level mutations to the logical replication write-ahead log

components.name: CDC Connector Engine
components.purpose: Streams WAL changes as structured JSON event messages into partitioned Kafka topics

components.name: Streaming Event Broker
components.purpose: Buffers database change events with key-based partitioning ensuring order per entity ID

components.name: Search Synchronization Consumer
components.purpose: Consumes CDC events, deduplicates records, and updates search index documents idempotently

components.name: Containerized Infrastructure
components.purpose: Orchestrates PostgreSQL, Kafka broker, Debezium Connect, and Elasticsearch containers

architecture.data_flow: An application executes INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE operations in PostgreSQL; the PostgreSQL WAL records the transaction; the Debezium connector captures the mutation and produces a structured event to Kafka; Python consumer processes read the topic; consumers enforce idempotent upserts into Elasticsearch using entity IDs as document identifiers; search queries immediately reflect the latest database state.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Idempotent consumer upserts using PostgreSQL primary keys as Elasticsearch document IDs; Kafka key partitioning ensuring strict per-record ordering.

targets.method: Timestamp delta measurement between PostgreSQL commit and Elasticsearch document indexing
targets.input: 1,000 synthetic database mutation transactions streamed at 100 operations per second
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, 8GB RAM, Docker Compose
targets.report: Latency benchmark summary table and timestamp difference histogram

targets.method: Injection of 500 duplicate Kafka message offsets into consumer group
targets.input: 1,000 unique entity mutations with 500 deliberately redelivered duplicate payloads
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Docker Compose environment
targets.minimum_pass: Downstream Elasticsearch document count equals exactly 1,000 with 0 duplicate records
targets.target: Downstream Elasticsearch document count equals exactly 1,000 with 0 duplicate records
targets.report: Verification script report comparing source table count with index count

targets.method: High-volume batch insertion load test measuring processed CDC events per second
targets.input: 20,000 synthetic row insertions executed via bulk transaction script
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, 8GB RAM, local SSD storage
targets.minimum_pass: Sustained pipeline capture throughput > 1,000 events/sec without connector lag buildup
targets.target: Sustained pipeline capture throughput > 2,500 events/sec without connector lag buildup
targets.report: Debezium metrics log reporting source-record-poll-rate and consumer lag

starter_input.spec: E-commerce product catalog schema in PostgreSQL with products, inventory, and categories tables.
starter_input.size: 5,000 initial product records and synthetic mutation generator producing 20,000 updates
starter_input.seeded_cases: Rapid multi-column updates, out-of-order event arrivals, schema column addition (ALTER TABLE), and transaction aborts
starter_input.label_source: Deterministic SQL migration scripts and Python test generators with fixed seed 8821
starter_input.personal_data_policy: Strictly mock synthetic product catalog and inventory data; no personal user information used

prerequisites: Intermediate Python programming and async IO concepts
Relational database administration basics (PostgreSQL WAL, replication slots)
Familiarity with event streaming concepts (Kafka topics, partitions, consumer groups)

environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts or paid API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Engine 24+ and Docker Compose installed
environment.fallback_path: Local SQLite WAL polling mock pipeline without Docker if container resources are constrained

riskiest_component.name: PostgreSQL Replication Slot Disk Saturation during Consumer Inactivity
riskiest_component.fallback: Configure max_slot_wal_keep_size in postgresql.conf to bound WAL retention on local disk

deliverables: Git repository containing Docker Compose files, Debezium connector configurations, and Python consumers
SQL migration scripts creating source schemas and test transaction generators
Benchmark script measuring end-to-end synchronization latency and throughput
Screener verification script executing pipeline tests and dynamic record validation in under 3 minutes
out_of_scope: Real-time stream processing with Apache Flink
resources: Apache Kafka consumer group and partition rebalancing architecture guide
PostgreSQL documentation on logical decoding and write-ahead logging

rubric.action: Check health of PostgreSQL, Kafka, and Debezium containers
rubric.expected_result: All containers report healthy and Debezium connector status shows RUNNING
rubric.pass_criterion: Connector state equals RUNNING with 1/1 tasks running and exit code 0

rubric.input: SQL INSERT statement executed in PostgreSQL products table
rubric.action: Query Elasticsearch products index for newly inserted record
rubric.expected_result: Elasticsearch returns matching document within 1,500ms of database commit
rubric.pass_criterion: Document matches PostgreSQL row fields with exit code 0

rubric.input: Injection of 500 duplicate Kafka messages into product CDC topic
rubric.expected_result: Consumer idempotently handles duplicates without creating duplicate Elasticsearch documents
rubric.pass_criterion: Final document count exactly equals source table count with 0 duplicates

rubric.input: High-volume batch load of 1,000 mutations across 10 seconds
rubric.expected_result: Benchmark script measures end-to-end latency for each transaction
rubric.pass_criterion: Measured p95 end-to-end sync latency is < 1,500ms across all mutations

rubric.expected_result: Script executes SQL update, monitors Kafka offset, and confirms dynamic SKU in Elasticsearch
rubric.pass_criterion: Script confirms dynamic record reflected in search index within 2 seconds with exit code 0

worksheet.q1: The student builds a Change Data Capture pipeline using Debezium to stream PostgreSQL write-ahead log mutations into Kafka, synchronizing a downstream Elasticsearch search index idempotently.
worksheet.q2: Core path: PostgreSQL logical replication, Debezium connector, Kafka streaming, Python idempotent consumer, and Elasticsearch sync (29h). Extended path: Transactional outbox router and Schema Registry integration (+14h).
worksheet.q3: Components: PostgreSQL WAL (4h), Debezium Connect (5h), Python Consumer (4h), Elasticsearch Sync (4h), Benchmark & Chaos (4h), Docs & Buffer (4h). Total 25h x 1.15 = 29h.
worksheet.q4: Project types: Data pipeline/ETL/streaming, Distributed systems. Metrics: End-to-End Change Propagation Latency, Idempotent Deduplication Invariant, Ingestion Throughput. Rejected: GPU inference throughput.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: PostgreSQL replication slot disk retention, consumer duplicate handling, schema evolution handling, and event ordering across partitions.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: synthetic product catalog schema with 5,000 initial records and update script producing 20,000 mutations. No personal data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: SQLite WAL mock without Docker.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Replication slot WAL disk buildup. Fallback: configure max_slot_wal_keep_size.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: pre-populated Elasticsearch index. Anti-fake check 5 inserts a dynamic random product SKU at runtime and verifies live end-to-end synchronization.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic e-commerce catalog data only.
